chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a bull that disobeyed (resisted slaughter): they rushed at it with their swords and named (said Bismillah), then they came to Ali (peace be upon him) and he said: 'This is a valid slaughter and its meat is permissible.'

key_terms.تَعَاصَى: To disobey/resist — the bull's active resistance that made normal slaughter impossible
key_terms.ذَكَاةٌ: Ritual slaughter (dhakah/tadhkiya) — the Islamic method of slaughtering animals
key_terms.سَمَّوْا: They named/invoked — i.e., said 'Bismillah' (In the name of God) before striking
key_terms.وَحِيَّةٌ: Valid/vivid — meaning the slaughter is recognized as legally sound despite the non-standard method

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the meat of an animal that was killed with a sword when it resisted slaughter?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a legal ruling attributed to Imam Ali (AS): when a bull resisted normal slaughter and people were compelled to strike it with swords while invoking the name of Allah (saying Bismillah), Imam Ali ruled the slaughter to be valid and the meat permissible. This hadith establishes an important principle in Islamic slaughter law — that invoking Allah's name (tasmiyya) and the intent to slaughter are essential, and when an animal cannot be slaughtered by the standard method due to resistance, alternative means with the conditions of tasmiyya are still valid.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said regarding a bull which disobeyed. So they pursued it with their swords, and Named (Bismillah), and they came to Aliasws. So heasws said: ‘This is a vivid slaughter, and its flesh is Permissible’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ‘Uthman from Ali has narrated from his father from-Fadl ibn ‘Abd al-Malik and ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that certain people once came to the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and said that their cow became difficult with them and they had only to subdue it with their sword. He (the Messenger of Allah) commanded them to use it for food.’”
